mainTopic: The sources for disqualifying רובע ונרבע, נעבד, מוקצה and נוגח from the מזבח, and the definition of מוקצה
overview: The גמרא works through a ברייתא that reads ויקרא 1:2 word by word, with each word disqualifying a type of animal from being a קרבן. רב אשי explains why רובע ונרבע cannot be learned by קל וחומר from a בעל מום: a בעל מום's blemish is visible, but רובע ונרבע's is not. That is why 'מן הבהמה' is needed. Next, 'מן הבקר' excludes a נעבד. The גמרא shows that a קל וחומר from אתנן ומחיר could be flipped, so a פסוק is needed here too. It then explains why the two words cannot be swapped, and רבי שמעון explains why the Torah needs to exclude both רובע and נוגח. A different תנא, the school of רבי ישמעאל, learns these disqualifications from the word השחתה in the blemish verse. The גמרא then shows how each תנא finds a source for excluding sick, old and filthy animals. Finally, ריש לקיש rules that only an animal set aside for seven years is a forbidden מוקצה, based on גדעון's bull. That leads to רבא's answer, which cites רבי אבא בר כהנא's teaching that eight normally forbidden things were allowed to גדעון that night, a list that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב אשי: the comparison to a blemished animal breaks down at its base
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the קל וחומר from a בעל מום to רובע ונרבע fails from the start. A בעל מום is disqualified because its blemish is visible.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Because you can say that the logic is broken from its very starting point. What is special about a blemished animal? Its blemish can be seen.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains why we cannot learn the law of רובע ונרבע from a בעל מום through a קל וחומר. The case we start from, the בעל מום, has a special feature that רובע ונרבע lacks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the starting case has nothing extra that could explain its law. A בעל מום has a visible defect, and that alone could be the reason it is unfit. A רובע ונרבע looks perfectly normal, so the starting case is not really 'weaker' in the way the קל וחומר needs.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation; a point that knocks down a proposed argument
From the very base of the logical argument
An animal with a physical blemish, which is unfit as a קרבן
Its blemish is visible and noticeable

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying a בעל מום is a lighter case. He is saying it has its own unique reason to be unfit, the visible blemish, so you cannot build from it to רובע ונרבע.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Because one can say
there is a refutation from the very base of the argument —
What is special about a blemished animal?
That its blemish is visible.

steps.triggerLanguage: משום דאיכא למימר מעיקרא דדינא פירכא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question of why רובע ונרבע needs a פסוק when it could seemingly be learned by קל וחומר from a בעל מום.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a unique feature of the base case (visible blemish) that undermines the קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: You could learn רובע ונרבע from a בעל מום by קל וחומר, so no פסוק would be needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קל וחומר fails because a בעל מום has a visible blemish, which רובע ונרבע does not.

steps.title: So the verse 'from the animals' is needed to exclude these animals
steps.stepSummary: Since a רובע ונרבע has no visible blemish, you might think it is fit for the מזבח. So the Torah writes 'מן הבהמה' to disqualify it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Would you say the same about an animal that mated with a person, or that a person mated with, whose blemish cannot be seen? Since its blemish cannot be seen, maybe it should be fit for the altar. That is why the verse says 'from the animals', to exclude these animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב אשי's point. Without a פסוק we might have thought a רובע ונרבע is fit, so the Torah had to say 'מן הבהמה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the first branch. Once the קל וחומר falls apart, logic alone could even point toward allowing the animal, since nothing about it looks wrong. That is exactly why the Torah needed to state the disqualification.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that mated with a person
An animal that a person mated with
Fit to be offered on the altar
The verse teaches; introduces the פסוק that settles the matter

steps.whatToRemember: רובע ונרבע cannot be learned from a בעל מום, because only the בעל מום's flaw is visible. So we need the פסוק 'מן הבהמה'.

phrases.english: Would you say the same about an animal that mated with a person or was mated with by a person,
whose blemish is not visible?
Since its blemish is not visible,
it should be fit for the altar —
therefore the verse says: 'From the animals,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:2

phrases.english: to exclude an animal that mated with a person or was mated with by a person.

steps.triggerLanguage: תאמר ברובע ונרבע שאין מומו ניכר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical result of רב אשי's refutation: the פסוק is truly needed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פסוק 'מן הבהמה' is needed to disqualify רובע ונרבע, because logic alone could have made it fit.

steps.title: 'From the herd' excludes a worshipped animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא's next phrase. 'מן הבקר' disqualifies a נעבד, an animal that was worshipped as an idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'From the cattle' comes to exclude an animal that was worshipped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next clause of the ברייתא. The words 'מן הבקר' teach that an animal people worshipped cannot be a קרבן. This sets up the next question: why is a פסוק needed for this?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic within the same ברייתא. It moves from רובע ונרבע to a נעבד. The rule is stated simply here, and the following steps test whether it could have been learned without the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that was itself worshipped as an idol
To exclude; to remove from the category

phrases.english: 'From the herd' —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:2, the same פסוק as before, now read word by word.

phrases.english: comes to exclude an animal that was worshipped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the same ברייתא, after the רובע ונרבע discussion has finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal that was worshipped is disqualified as a קרבן, learned from 'מן הבקר'.

steps.title: Couldn't we learn this from a prostitute's fee and a dog's price?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a קל וחומר. אתנן ומחיר are forbidden even though their decorations are allowed. So a נעבד, whose decoration is forbidden, should surely be forbidden too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can't this be learned by logic? A prostitute's fee and a dog's price have decorations that are allowed, yet the animals themselves are forbidden. A worshipped animal's decoration is forbidden, so isn't it logical that the animal itself is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we need the פסוק 'מן הבקר' at all. It suggests we could figure out the law of a נעבד by a קל וחומר from אתנן ומחיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decoration on an אתנן or מחיר may be used in the מקדש, which makes them the more lenient case, and yet the animals themselves are forbidden. A נעבד is stricter, because even its decoration is forbidden. So it seems obvious that the animal itself should be forbidden, and the פסוק looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it logical? Introduces a proposed קל וחומר
An animal given as payment to a prostitute
An animal received in exchange for a dog
The coating or decoration added to the animal

phrases.english: But isn't it logical?
If a prostitute's fee and a dog's price,
whose coatings are permitted —
phrases.notes: The coating is decoration placed on the animal, like gold. Here it may be used for the מקדש.

phrases.english: are themselves forbidden,
then a worshipped animal, whose coating is forbidden —
isn't it logical that it itself is forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: והלא דין הוא ומה אתנן ומחיר שציפויין מותרין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the פסוק just quoted in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the פסוק 'מן הבקר' to disqualify a נעבד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from אתנן ומחיר, which are lenient about their coating but still forbidden, seems to make a נעבד forbidden without any פסוק.

steps.title: The logic can be reversed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the קל וחומר. אתנן ומחיר are forbidden themselves, yet their coatings are allowed. So a נעבד, which is not forbidden by an explicit verse, should have its coating allowed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or reverse it: a prostitute's fee and a dog's price are forbidden, yet their coatings are permitted. A worshipped animal is permitted, so shouldn't its coating be permitted too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the קל וחומר by running it in the opposite direction. That shows logic alone cannot decide the law here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now אתנן ומחיר are treated as the stricter case, since the Torah explicitly forbids the animals themselves. A נעבד is treated as more lenient, since no verse would forbid it. Because the argument works both ways, the original קל וחומר is not reliable, and this sets up the need for a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Reversal; running the same argument in the opposite direction

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not actually believe a נעבד is permitted. It only shows that, without the פסוק, logic could point either way, so the פסוק is needed.

phrases.english: Or reverse it:
If a prostitute's fee and a dog's price,
which are themselves forbidden —
have coatings that are permitted,
then a worshipped animal, which is permitted —
phrases.notes: Here we pretend no verse forbids it, so it would count as permitted.

phrases.english: shouldn't its coating be permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undercuts the קל וחומר of step 4 by showing it can be reversed.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the קל וחומר proposed in step 4 as a way to learn that a נעבד is forbidden
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument can be flipped: using the same two cases, one could conclude that a נעבד and its coating are both permitted.

steps.title: The flipped argument would cancel a verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the flipped קל וחומר. If the coating of a worshipped thing were allowed, the פסוק forbidding the silver and gold on idols would mean nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, you have cancelled the פסוק: 'Do not desire the silver and gold on them and take it for yourself!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the flipped קל וחומר from step 5. That argument said the coating of a נעבד should be allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The flipped קל וחומר ended with: a נעבד's coating is permitted. But the Torah clearly forbids the silver and gold that covers idols. An argument that cancels an explicit פסוק cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: You have cancelled (made a פסוק meaningless)
Do not desire. Here it means the ban on the silver and gold covering idols
The coating or covering (decoration) on an object

phrases.english: If so, you have cancelled
phrases.notes: 'If so' means: if a worshipped thing's coating is allowed, as the flipped argument in step 5 said.

phrases.english: 'Do not desire the silver and gold on them
phrases.notes: דברים 7:25

phrases.english: and take it for yourself'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the flipped קל וחומר of step 5 by showing it clashes with a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion of the flipped קל וחומר that a נעבד's coating is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A logical argument cannot permit something an explicit פסוק forbids. The silver and gold on idols is forbidden.

steps.title: The verse covers non-living idols, so a living animal needs its own source
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about silver and gold is about non-living idols. For a living animal, which is itself permitted, you might think its coating is permitted too. So 'מן הבקר' is needed to exclude a נעבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: I can still keep that פסוק: 'Do not desire the silver and gold' is about something without a living spirit. But with something that has a living spirit, since the animal itself is permitted, I might think its coating is also permitted. So the Torah says 'מן הבקר', to exclude the worshipped animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the flipped argument by limiting the פסוק to non-living idols. This explains why the ברייתא needed 'מן הבקר' for a worshipped animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The silver-and-gold פסוק still has a job: non-living idols. A living animal is different, because the animal itself stays permitted, so its coating might also seem permitted. That is exactly why the ברייתא needed 'מן הבקר' to exclude a נעבד.

keyTerms.meaning: I will keep it (show the פסוק still has a use)
A living spirit, meaning a living creature
Since
Therefore the Torah says (introduces the פסוק that teaches the rule)
To exclude

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the silver-and-gold פסוק is being thrown out. It still fully applies to idols that are not alive. Only the case of a living worshipped animal needed the extra words 'מן הבקר'.

phrases.english: I will keep it [in force]:
'Do not desire the silver and gold' —
is about something that has no living spirit,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּדָבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ רוּחַ חַיִּים,
phrases.english: but with something that has a living spirit,
since it is permitted —
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'they' (in round brackets). The square brackets give the corrected wording, 'it', meaning the animal itself.

phrases.english: I might think the coating should be permitted?
So the Torah says 'from the herd' —
to exclude the worshipped animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by narrowing the פסוק to non-living idols.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The silver-and-gold פסוק covers every worshipped thing, so the flipped argument contradicts it.
steps.terutzMaskana: That פסוק covers only non-living idols. A living worshipped animal needs 'מן הבקר' to be excluded.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the ברייתא in step 3 needed a פסוק for a נעבד instead of relying on a קל וחומר.

steps.title: רב חנניא: another verse already forbids the coating
steps.stepSummary: רב חנניא objects: the answer implies the coating would be permitted without 'מן הבקר'. But 'ואבדתם את שמם' teaches that everything made for idols must be destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנניא challenged this: the only reason is that the פסוק excluded it. So if the פסוק had not excluded it, the coating would be permitted? But it is written, 'and you shall destroy their name', meaning everything made for them!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנניא challenges the answer of step 7. He points to another פסוק that seems to already forbid the coating of any idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 implied that without 'מן הבקר', a worshipped animal's coating would be permitted. רב חנניא says that cannot be. 'ואבדתם את שמם' already requires destroying anything made for idol worship, including a coating.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it (raised a strong objection)
The reason
The פסוק excluded it
And you shall destroy their name

phrases.english: Rav Chananya challenged this:
The reason is that the verse excluded it,
so if the verse had not excluded it —
the coating would be permitted?
But it is written, 'and you shall destroy their name' —
phrases.notes: דברים 12:3

phrases.english: everything made for them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks what step 7 implies: that the coating would be permitted without 'מן הבקר'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of step 7 that, without 'מן הבקר', a living worshipped animal's coating would be permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'ואבדתם את שמם' already forbids everything made for idols. So no special פסוק should be needed, and the coating could never be permitted.

steps.title: 'Destroy their name' means giving idols insulting nicknames
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'ואבדתם את שמם' teaches something different: we must call idols and their places by insulting names. It gives three examples.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק comes to teach that we give them a nickname. A 'House of Elevation' we call a 'House of Destruction'. 'Face of the King' becomes 'Face of a Dog'. 'All-Seeing Eye' becomes 'Eye of a Thorn'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב חנניא. The פסוק he quoted is not about forbidding coatings. It is about giving idols insulting names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חנניא read 'their name' as 'everything made for them'. The גמרא reads 'destroy their name' literally: wipe out their honored names by replacing them with insulting ones. So that פסוק says nothing about coatings, and 'מן הבקר' is still needed.

keyTerms.meaning: To give a nickname
'House of Elevation', the idol worshippers' honored name for a place
'House of Destruction', the insulting nickname we use instead

steps.whatToRemember: A living worshipped animal (נעבד) is excluded from the מזבח by 'מן הבקר'. The silver-and-gold פסוק covers non-living idols. 'ואבדתם את שמם' teaches us to give idols insulting names, not a rule about coatings.

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא לְכַנּוֹת לָהֶם שֵׁם הוּא דַּאֲתָא:
phrases.english: That [verse] comes to give them a nickname:
a 'House of Elevation' is called a 'House of Destruction',
'Face of the King' — 'Face of a Dog',
'All-Seeing Eye' — 'Eye of a Thorn'.

steps.triggerLanguage: ההוא לכנות להם שם הוא דאתא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חנניא's challenge by giving his פסוק a different meaning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the פסוק to a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ואבדתם את שמם' forbids everything made for idols, so 'מן הבקר' would be unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ואבדתם את שמם' teaches giving idols insulting nicknames, so the rule about a worshipped animal still comes from 'מן הבקר'.

steps.title: Why not swap the two exclusions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests reversing the ברייתא: let 'מן הבהמה' exclude a נעבד and 'מן הבקר' exclude רובע ונרבע.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe I can flip it: 'from the בהמה' comes to exclude a worshipped animal, and 'from the בקר' comes to exclude an animal that had relations with a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא matched each exclusion to its specific word. Why not switch them around?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said 'מן הבהמה' excludes רובע ונרבע and 'מן הבקר' excludes a נעבד. Both words are extra, so each could seem to exclude either case. The גמרא wants a reason for the ברייתא's exact matching.

keyTerms.meaning: I will reverse it (switch the two derivations)
An animal that had relations with a person (it was the active one)
An animal that a person had relations with (it was the passive one)
An animal that was worshipped as an idol
To exclude

phrases.english: But I can reverse it:
'From the cattle' comes to exclude the worshipped animal,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:2. This is the reverse of what the ברייתא said.

phrases.english: and 'from the herd' comes to exclude an animal that lay with a person and one that a person lay with!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the basic ברייתא pairing of words to exclusions, which the earlier steps assumed, and questions it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's assignment of רובע ונרבע to 'מן הבהמה' and נעבד to 'מן הבקר'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both words are extra and neither seems tied to a specific case, so the assignments could be swapped.

steps.title: Each word matches the verse where it appears
steps.stepSummary: The Torah uses the word בהמה when it discusses relations with an animal, and תהלים uses שור (an animal of the בקר) when it describes the golden calf. So each word excludes its own matching topic.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it comes from the context of the verses. About a 'בהמה' it is written: 'If a man lies with a בהמה, he shall surely be put to death.' About an animal of the בקר it is written: 'They exchanged their glory for the likeness of an ox that eats grass.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the matching is not random. Each word is linked to the topic where the תנ"ך uses that same kind of animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law of relations with an animal is written with the word בהמה, so 'מן הבהמה' excludes רובע ונרבע. The sin of idol worship, the golden calf, is described with a שור, which is an animal of the בקר, so 'מן הבקר' excludes a נעבד. Because of this, the derivations cannot be flipped.

keyTerms.meaning: From the context (subject matter) of the verse
Regarding, in connection with
The likeness of an ox, referring to the golden calf

steps.whatToRemember: בהמה goes with רובע ונרבע because of the verse about relations with an animal. בקר goes with נעבד because of the golden calf, the 'ox that eats grass'.

phrases.english: There, it is derived from the context of the verse;
phrases.notes: 'There' means the ברייתא's matching. Each word is tied to where the תנ"ך uses that same kind of animal.

phrases.english: regarding a 'beast' it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְאִישׁ כִּי יִתֵּן שְׁכׇבְתּוֹ בִּבְהֵמָה מוֹת יוּמָת״,
phrases.english: 'And if a man lies with a beast, he shall surely be put to death';
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:15

phrases.english: regarding the herd it is written:
'Thus they exchanged their glory'
'for the likeness of an ox that eats grass.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 106:20. This verse is about the golden calf, and an ox is an animal of the בקר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request to reverse the derivations.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Contextual linkage: each extra word is tied to the topic where the תנ"ך uses that same animal term.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two words are interchangeable, so the exclusions could be swapped.
steps.terutzMaskana: בהמה matches relations with an animal (ויקרא 20) and בקר matches idol worship (the golden calf), so the ברייתא's matching stands.

steps.title: The flock excludes מוקצה and נוגח
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: 'מן הצאן' excludes an animal set aside for idol worship, and the extra 'ו' in 'ומן הצאן' excludes an animal that gored.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'From the flock' comes to exclude the animal set aside for idolatry. 'And from the flock' comes to exclude the goring animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quoting the ברייתא, which continues through the rest of the פסוק. Two more kinds of animal are excluded from being a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מן הצאן' exclude a מוקצה. The extra letter ו ('and') adds one more exclusion, a נוגח. This sets up רבי שמעון's question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal set aside to be used for idol worship
An animal that gored and killed a person
Flock (sheep and goats)

phrases.english: 'From the flock' comes to exclude the animal set aside,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:2. 'Set aside' means set aside for idol worship.

phrases.english: 'And from the flock' comes to exclude the goring animal.
phrases.notes: The extra letter ו ('and') is what teaches this exclusion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the ברייתא again after the side discussion about swapping derivations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מוקצה and a נוגח are disqualified as קרבנות, learned from 'מן הצאן' and 'ומן הצאן'.

steps.title: Why does the Torah need both רובע and נוגח?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון asks: if the Torah excludes a רובע, why also a נוגח, and if a נוגח, why also a רובע?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: If רובע is stated, why is נוגח stated? And if נוגח is stated, why is רובע stated?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון asks why we need two separate exclusions. Both seem to teach the same kind of rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both a רובע and a נוגח are animals that caused a sin or death involving a person, and both are put to death. So it seems that learning one should teach the other. He is setting up his explanation that each has something unique.

keyTerms.meaning: Why was it stated? (Why does the Torah need to say this?)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון does not disagree with the ruling. He agrees both are disqualified and only asks why the Torah needed to teach both separately.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם נֶאֱמַר רוֹבֵעַ — לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר נוֹגֵחַ?
phrases.english: If an animal that lay with a person is stated, why is a goring animal stated?

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם נֶאֱמַר נוֹגֵחַ — לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר רוֹבֵעַ?
phrases.english: And if a goring animal is stated, why is an animal that lay with a person stated?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם נֶאֱמַר רוֹבֵעַ לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר נוֹגֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the ברייתא needs both the רובע exclusion (from בהמה) and the נוגח exclusion (from 'ומן הצאן').
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What each case has that the other lacks, so that both exclusions are needed.

steps.title: With רובע, forced counts like willing
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון explains that each case has its own special stringency. With רובע, an animal that was forced is treated like one that acted willingly, which is not true of a נוגח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because there is something in רובע that is not in נוגח. In רובע there is this: with רובע, forced is treated like willing, which is not so with a goring animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון answers his own question. He shows a stringency that רובע has and נוגח does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With רובע, the animal is disqualified even if a person forced the act. With a נוגח, an animal that was pushed to gore is not treated the same way. So we could not learn רובע from נוגח. The next step gives the other direction of his answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Forced, done under compulsion
Willingly, of its own accord
Which is not so (in the other case)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic way the Torah justifies two similar laws: each one has a unique feature, so neither can be learned from the other.

phrases.english: Because there is something in an animal that lay with a person
that is not so in a goring animal, and the reverse.
There is a stringency in an animal that lay with a person:
with an animal that lay with a person, forced is treated like willing,
which is not so with a goring animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ בָּרוֹבֵעַ מָה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן בַּנּוֹגֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי שמעון's question from the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רובע has a stringency, forced counts like willing, that נוגח lacks. So נוגח could not teach רובע, and both exclusions are needed.

steps.title: The goring animal has its own stringency, so both cases are needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון finishes his answer. A נוגח has a stringency that a רובע lacks, because its owner pays כופר. So the Torah had to state both.
steps.simpleTranslation: A goring animal has a stringency: its owner pays a ransom, which is not true of an animal that mounted a person. So the Torah needed to mention the רובע, and it also needed to mention the נוגח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון completes his answer from the previous step by showing the special stringency of a נוגח. He concludes that neither case could be learned from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 he showed that רובע is stricter in one way: forced acts count like willing ones. Now he shows that נוגח is stricter in another way: the owner pays כופר. Since each case is stricter in its own way, you could not learn one from the other, so both exclusions are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Ransom the owner pays when his ox kills a person
An animal that gored
It was necessary to state; neither case could be learned from the other

steps.whatToRemember: Two cases each with a different stringency cannot be learned from each other, so the Torah has to write both.

phrases.english: There is a stringency with a goring animal,
that for a goring animal, the owner pays the ransom,
phrases.notes: This is the ransom the owner pays when his ox kills a person (שמות 21:30).

phrases.english: which is not so with an animal that mounted a person.
So it was necessary to state the animal that mounted a person,
and it was necessary to state the goring animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּצְרַךְ לוֹמַר רוֹבֵעַ, וְהוּצְרַךְ לוֹמַר נוֹגֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי שמעון's answer begun in step 14 by giving the second half of the comparison.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A נוגח's owner pays כופר, which a רובע's owner does not, so each case has its own stringency and both must be written.

steps.title: Another תנא's source: רובע ונרבע are like a blemish before consecration
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that a different תנא learns the law of רובע ונרבע from another place. His ברייתא says they are like קדשים whose temporary blemish came before their consecration.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this תנא brings it from here, as was taught in a ברייתא: An animal that mounted a person and an animal that was mounted, etc., are like sacrificial animals whose temporary blemish came before their consecration.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now opens a new source: a different ברייתא that also disqualifies רובע ונרבע. This step sets up the ruling, and the source verse comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our ברייתא learned the law of רובע ונרבע from 'מן הבהמה'. This other תנא treats these animals like animals that had a passing blemish when they were consecrated. Such an animal can never go on the altar, but it still has a holiness that cannot simply be removed.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that a person had relations with
A temporary blemish that will heal
Animals consecrated as sacrifices
Consecration; making something holy for the Temple

phrases.english: And this תנא brings it from here,
phrases.notes: "It" is the rule that a רובע ונרבע cannot be offered. This תנא learns it from a different source than our ברייתא.

phrases.english: as it was taught in a ברייתא:
An animal that mounted a person and an animal that was mounted by a person
(and all of them) [etc.].
phrases.notes: Some versions say "and all of them". The corrected wording in square brackets says "etc.", meaning the list goes on.

phrases.english: they are like sacrificial animals
whose temporary blemish came before their consecration.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי תַּנָּא מַיְיתֵי לַהּ מֵהָכָא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the first ברייתא's 'מן הבהמה' derivation and brings a different תנא's source for the same law.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רובע ונרבע are treated like קדשים whose temporary blemish came before their consecration.

steps.title: They need a permanent blemish to be redeemed, with the verse
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: such animals can be redeemed only after they get a permanent blemish. It quotes 'כי משחתם בהם מום בם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they need a permanent blemish to be redeemed on account of it, as it says: 'Because their corruption is in them, there is a blemish in them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its ruling. It explains that these animals cannot be redeemed until they get a permanent blemish, and it brings a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the animals are like ones with a temporary blemish, they cannot be offered and also cannot be redeemed yet. Only a permanent blemish allows redemption. The ברייתא quotes a verse about blemished animals, which sets up the גמרא's next question.

keyTerms.meaning: A permanent blemish
To redeem; to take the holiness off the animal by exchanging it for money
Their corruption

steps.confusionAlert: The verse quoted here seems to be only about physical blemishes, not about רובע ונרבע. That is exactly what the גמרא asks next.

phrases.english: And they need a permanent blemish
to be redeemed on account of it,
as it is said:
"Because their corruption is in them, there is a blemish in them."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:25

steps.triggerLanguage: וּצְרִיכִין מוּם קָבוּעַ לִפְדּוֹת עֲלֵיהֶן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and gives its source verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רובע ונרבע that were consecrated cannot be redeemed until they get a permanent blemish.

steps.title: How does this verse teach about רובע ונרבע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the derivation is, since the verse seems to talk about blemishes, not about רובע ונרבע.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the derivation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the quoted פסוק connects to רובע ונרבע. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse speaks of 'a blemish in them', but רובע ונרבע have no physical blemish. The גמרא wants to know where this verse hints at them at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The derivation; what we learn from the verse

phrases.english: What is the derivation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the verse quoted in step 17 relates to the case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the verse 'כי משחתם בהם מום בם' teaches anything about רובע ונרבע.

steps.title: Words are missing: הַשְׁחָתָה means ערוה and עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ברייתא is missing words. The verse is the source that רובע ונרבע are forbidden, because the school of רבי ישמעאל taught that הַשְׁחָתָה always refers to ערוה and עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא is missing words, and this is what it teaches: From where do we know that they are forbidden? The verse says: 'Because their corruption is in them, there is a blemish in them.' And the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: every place where 'corruption' is said, it means only sexual sin and idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by filling in missing words in the ברייתא. The verse proves that רובע ונרבע are forbidden, because the word 'corruption' points to sexual sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse is not the source for needing a permanent blemish. It is the source that these animals are forbidden at all. The word 'משחתם' (their corruption) is the key, since the school of רבי ישמעאל taught that הַשְׁחָתָה always means ערוה or עבודה זרה, and a רובע ונרבע was involved in ערוה.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing words; the גמרא fills them in
The verse says; introduces the source
Corruption
Forbidden sexual relations
Idol worship

steps.whatToRemember: This תנא learns that a רובע ונרבע is unfit from the word 'משחתם', because הַשְׁחָתָה in the Torah means ערוה or עבודה זרה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of the school of רבי ישמעאל about הַשְׁחָתָה gives a word-based source for disqualifying both kinds of animals, those involved in ערוה and those involved in עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: It is missing words,
and this is what it teaches:
From where do we know that they are forbidden?
phrases.notes: "They" means the רובע ונרבע: forbidden to be brought as a sacrifice.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"Because their corruption is in them, there is a blemish in them,"
and the school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
Every place where 'corruption' is said,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא דְּבַר עֶרְוָה וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
phrases.english: it means only sexual sin and idol worship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by filling in missing words in the ברייתא and explaining the word משחתם.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse is the source that רובע ונרבע are forbidden, because הַשְׁחָתָה always refers to ערוה and עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Proof verses that השחתה means ערוה and עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings two פסוקים showing that the word השחתה is used for ערוה and for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ערוה: as it says, 'for all flesh had corrupted' its way. עבודה זרה: as it says, 'lest you act corruptly and make for yourselves a carved idol, the form of any figure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל from step 19 with two פסוקים. One shows that השחתה is used for ערוה, and the other shows it is used for עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 claimed that the word השחתה always points to ערוה and עבודה זרה. Here are the proofs. The דור המבול 'corrupted' their way, which refers to ערוה, and the warning about making an idol uses the same root, which refers to עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: a matter of forbidden relations; here this includes an animal used for bestiality
corrupted; the same root as הַשְׁחָתָה
a carved idol
as it is written

phrases.english: A matter of sexual immorality — as it is written:
"For all flesh had corrupted," etc.
phrases.notes: בראשית ו:יב, about the generation of the flood.

phrases.english: Idol worship — as it is written:
"Lest you act corruptly and make for yourselves
a carved idol, the form of any figure."
phrases.notes: דברים ד:טז

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the proof verses for the rule quoted in step 19 that השחתה refers to ערוה and עבודה זרה.
steps.raayaObject: That the word השחתה refers to ערוה and to עבודה זרה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית ו:יב (ערוה) and דברים ד:טז (עבודה זרה).

steps.title: Whatever a blemish disqualifies, ערוה and עבודה זרה disqualify too
steps.stepSummary: Since the blemish verse uses the word השחתה, ערוה and עבודה זרה disqualify every animal that a מום would disqualify.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any animal that a blemish disqualifies, a matter of ערוה or עבודה זרה also disqualifies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the derivation. Wherever a blemish makes an animal unfit for the מזבח, ערוה and עבודה זרה make it unfit as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse 'כי משחתם בהם מום בם' puts השחתה right next to the word מום. Since השחתה means ערוה and עבודה זרה, the Torah is treating them like a blemish. That is how רובע ונרבע, מוקצה and נעבד become forbidden for the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: a physical blemish that makes an animal unfit for the מזבח
disqualifies

steps.whatToRemember: For the school of רבי ישמעאל, the source that רובע ונרבע (and animals used for עבודה זרה) are unfit is the word השחתה in the blemish verse. They are treated just like a blemished animal.

phrases.english: Any case in which a blemish disqualifies them —
a matter of sexual immorality and idol worship
disqualify them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the legal rule from the verses proven in step 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Any animal that a מום would disqualify is also disqualified by ערוה or עבודה זרה.

steps.title: How does the school of רבי ישמעאל use 'מן הבהמה מן הבקר ומן הצאן'?
steps.stepSummary: The other תנא learned these disqualifications from 'מן הבהמה מן הבקר ומן הצאן'. So what does the school of רבי ישמעאל learn from those words?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל: what does he learn from 'from the animal, from the cattle and from the flock'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question. If the school of רבי ישמעאל gets these rules from the blemish verse, what does it do with the words the other תנא used?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא used the extra words 'מן הבהמה מן הבקר ומן הצאן' to disqualify animals like רובע ונרבע. The school of רבי ישמעאל does not need them for that. The גמרא assumes no words of the Torah are wasted, so it asks what they teach for him.

keyTerms.meaning: the תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל
what does he expound from them?

phrases.english: And the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael:
"From the animal, from the cattle and from the flock"
phrases.notes: ויקרא א:ב. The earlier ברייתא used these words as its source for disqualifying these animals.

phrases.english: what does he expound from them?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל מַאי דָרֵישׁ בְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the school of רבי ישמעאל has a different source, the גמרא asks what it does with the first ברייתא's verse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the school of רבי ישמעאל learns from 'מן הבהמה מן הבקר ומן הצאן'.

steps.title: Those words exclude a sick, old or filthy animal
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל uses the three phrases to exclude a sick animal, an old animal and a filthy animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs them to exclude a sick animal, an old animal and a filthy animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the school of רבי ישמעאל uses these words for a different set of exclusions: sick, old and filthy animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the three phrases (מן הבהמה, מן הבקר, מן הצאן) excludes one kind of animal. So the words are not wasted for him; they simply teach a different law.

keyTerms.meaning: he needs it (for another teaching)
to exclude
sick
filthy, foul-smelling

phrases.english: He needs them
to exclude a sick, an old, and a filthy animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The school of רבי ישמעאל uses those words to exclude a sick, old or filthy animal.

steps.title: Where does the first תנא learn about sick, old and filthy animals?
steps.stepSummary: The first תנא used those words for רובע ונרבע. So where does he learn that a sick, old or filthy animal is unfit?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the first תנא, who used these verses for רובע ונרבע: where does he learn that a sick, old or filthy animal is unfit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question around. If the first תנא used those verses for רובע ונרבע, where does he get the exclusion of sick, old and filthy animals?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that a sick, old or filthy animal is unfit. The school of רבי ישמעאל already has a source for this. The first תנא used that verse for something else, so he needs another one.

keyTerms.meaning: the first תנא; here, the תנא of the earlier ברייתא
took them out; used them
an animal that had relations with a person, and an animal that was used that way
from where does he learn it?

phrases.english: And the first tanna,
who used these verses
for an animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality,
from where does he derive sick, old, and filthy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the mirror image of step 22, this time about the first תנא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The first תנא's source for excluding a sick, old or filthy animal.

steps.title: From 'מן הצאן מן הכבשים ומן העזים'
steps.stepSummary: The first תנא learns the exclusion of sick, old and filthy animals from a different verse: 'מן הצאן מן הכבשים ומן העזים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'from the flock, from the sheep and from the goats.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the first תנא uses a different verse, which also has three 'from' phrases, to exclude sick, old and filthy animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That verse has three 'מן' phrases, one for each of the three exclusions. So the first תנא has a source for every law, just like the school of רבי ישמעאל.

keyTerms.meaning: he derives it from
sheep
goats

phrases.english: He derives it from
"From the flock, from the sheep and from the goats."
phrases.notes: ויקרא א:י

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first תנא learns it from 'מן הצאן מן הכבשים ומן העזים'.

steps.title: For the school of רבי ישמעאל, that verse is ordinary Torah wording
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל does not learn anything from 'מן הצאן מן הכבשים ומן העזים', because this is simply how the Torah usually talks.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for the תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל, this is just the verse's normal way of speaking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: what does the school of רבי ישמעאל do with the first תנא's verse? It says those words are just the Torah's normal style, so there is nothing extra to learn from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah naturally names the general group (flock) and then its kinds (sheep, goats). For the school of רבי ישמעאל, that is ordinary phrasing and not extra words. This closes the loop, since each תנא now has one source for each law.

keyTerms.meaning: the normal way the verse speaks
to speak like this

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים agree on the laws. They differ only on which verse teaches what. The school of רבי ישמעאל learns רובע ונרבע from השחתה and sick, old and filthy from 'מן הבהמה מן הבקר ומן הצאן'. The first תנא learns רובע ונרבע from 'מן הבהמה' and sick, old and filthy from 'מן הצאן מן הכבשים ומן העזים'.

phrases.english: And according to the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael,
it is the manner of the verse to speak this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the school of רבי ישמעאל does not learn anything from the verse the first תנא used in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The school of רבי ישמעאל reads 'מן הצאן מן הכבשים ומן העזים' as ordinary wording, not as extra words to learn from.

steps.title: The משנה's question: what is a מוקצה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, which defines a מוקצה as an animal set aside for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: which animal is a מוקצה? One set aside for עבודה זרה, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה's definition of מוקצה. This line sets up ריש לקיש's statement that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about where the Torah teaches these disqualifications. Now the גמרא asks how to define one of them: how strongly must an animal be set aside for עבודה זרה before it counts as מוקצה?

keyTerms.meaning: an animal set aside (here, for עבודה זרה)
and so on; the rest of the quote

phrases.english: Which is the set-aside animal?
One set aside for idol worship, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of sources and opens a new topic based on the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מוקצה is an animal set aside for עבודה זרה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: only an animal set aside for seven years is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש limits the rule. Only an animal set aside for seven years counts as a forbidden מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: the only forbidden one is an animal set aside for seven years.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש makes the משנה's rule narrower. Not every animal set aside for עבודה זרה is forbidden for the מזבח, only one set aside for seven years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just said 'set aside for עבודה זרה' without giving any limit. ריש לקיש adds a condition, seven years, so an animal set aside in a lesser way would not be forbidden as מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: nothing is forbidden except
seven years

phrases.english: Reish Lakish says:
Nothing is prohibited except
an animal set aside for seven years.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: אֵין אָסוּר אֶלָּא מוּקְצֶה לְשֶׁבַע שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the משנה's definition of מוקצה quoted in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only an animal set aside for seven years is forbidden as מוקצה.

steps.title: The source: גדעון's bull of seven years
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about גדעון's 'second bull, of seven years' shows that people set an animal aside for seven years for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And that same night, ה׳ said to him: Take your father's bull, and the second bull, of seven years.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for ריש לקיש's rule from step 28. The source is the פסוק in שופטים about גדעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bull was raised for seven years to be used for בעל. That shows seven years was the normal amount of time for preparing an animal for עבודה זרה. That is why ריש לקיש says only seven years makes an animal a forbidden מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it says (introduces a פסוק as a source)
The second bull, the one raised for seven years
Seven years, the key words for ריש לקיש's rule

phrases.english: As it is stated: “And it came to pass that same night,
phrases.notes: שופטים 6:25

phrases.english: that [the Lord] said [to him]:
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the words in square brackets; the corrected wording adds them.

phrases.aramaic: קַח אֶת פַּר הַשּׁוֹר אֲשֶׁר לְאָבִיךָ
phrases.english: Take your father's bull,
and the second bull, of seven years.”
phrases.notes: 'Seven years' is the proof. This bull was raised for seven years for בעל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for ריש לקיש's seven-year rule.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's rule that only an animal set aside for seven years is a forbidden מוקצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: שופטים 6:25, the 'second bull, of seven years' of גדעון

steps.title: But that bull was actually worshipped
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that גדעון's bull was not only set aside. It was really worshipped.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there, was the bull only set aside? It was also actually worshipped!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof. גדעון's bull seems to have been actually worshipped, not just set aside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that was really worshipped (נעבד) is in a more severe category than one that was only set aside. So the case does not seem to be a clean example of מוקצה. It is also hard to understand how גדעון could offer a worshipped animal as a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal set aside for עבודה זרה but not yet worshipped
An animal that was actually worshipped as an idol
Only, merely

phrases.english: But there, was it only set aside?
phrases.notes: 'There' means גדעון's bull from the פסוק.

phrases.english: It was also actually worshipped!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof brought in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of גדעון's bull as an example of מוקצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the bull was actually worshipped, it was a נעבד and not just a מוקצה. Then it does not prove anything about מוקצה, and it is hard to see how it could be offered.

steps.title: It was set aside but never worshipped
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב answers that the bull was only set aside for worship. It was never actually worshipped.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: It was set aside to be worshipped, but they did not worship it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב answers the challenge. He says the bull was only prepared for worship and never actually used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this answer, the bull really was a מוקצה and not a נעבד. So the פסוק is a fitting source for ריש לקיש's seven-year rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Set aside in order to be worshipped
But they did not worship it

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said:
It was set aside to be worshipped, but they did not worship it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the bull was only set aside, not worshipped
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bull had been actually worshipped
steps.terutzMaskana: It was only מוקצה, so it fits ריש לקיש's rule

steps.title: It was worshipped, but this was a one-time exception
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the bull really was worshipped. Its use was a special one-time exception, based on רבי אבא בר כהנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, they did worship it, and this case is a special exception, like the teaching of רבי אבא בר כהנא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer. He agrees the bull was worshipped. He sets up the teaching of רבי אבא בר כהנא, which comes next, to explain why it was still allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not deny that the bull was a נעבד. He says that bringing it as a קרבן was a חידוש, a one-time exception that broke the normal rules. You cannot learn general rules from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth (keeps the original assumption)
A one-time exception; something new that does not follow the usual rules
In line with the teaching of a certain רבי

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying a worshipped animal can normally be offered. He is saying גדעון's case was a special exception that night.

phrases.english: Rava said: Really, they did worship it,
and it is a special exception,
in line with the teaching of Rabbi Abba bar Kahana,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer than רב אחא בר יעקב to the same קשיא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception: the case was a one-time חידוש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A worshipped bull could never be used, so the case must not involve worship
steps.terutzMaskana: It was worshipped, but that night was a special exception to the rules

steps.title: Eight things were permitted to גדעון that night
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר כהנא teaches that eight normally forbidden things were allowed that night. The first three are listed here.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אבא בר כהנא said: Eight things were permitted that night: offering outside the Temple, offering at night, and a non-כהן doing the service...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the teaching that רבא relied on. It begins listing the eight exceptions, and the list continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a קרבן must be brought in the proper place, during the day, and by a כהן. גדעון broke all of these rules that night by command of ה׳. This supports רבא's idea that using a worshipped bull was also part of these one-time exceptions.

keyTerms.meaning: Eight things
Offering outside the proper place of the משכן
Offering at night, which is normally invalid
A non-כהן doing the service

phrases.english: As Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said:
Eight things were permitted on that night:
phrases.notes: 'That night' is the night in the פסוק when גדעון tore down his father's altar to בעל.

phrases.english: outside, and night, and a non-priest,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the teaching that רבא referred to in step 32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eight normally forbidden things were permitted to גדעון that night, starting with offering outside the proper place, offering at night, and a non-כהן doing the service.
